--BEGIN AGENT OBSERVATION--
commit 759f6961
Author: John Marshall <jmarshall@hey.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 10 15:33:00 2022 +0100

    Recognise FASTA/Q even if the file has a very long header file

    The previous code only looked at the first 2048 bytes of the file, so
    FASTA/Q files with a header line longer than that were not recognised.
    This fixes samtools#1689.

    The fix is to use hts_getline() to read the first line, rather than
    looking at the initial peek buffer.

diff --git a/hts.c b/hts.c
index 4b0b0a2..e2d6ba44 100644
--- a/hts.c
+++ b/hts.c
@@ -170,7 +170,7 @@ static int is_fastaq(const unsigned char *u, const unsigned char *ulim)
     return (u == ulim || *u == '\r' || *u == '\n')? 1 : 0;
 }
 
-static int secondline_is_bases(const unsigned char *u, const unsigned char *ulim)
+static int is_fastaq(const unsigned char *u, const unsigned char *ulim)
 {
     // Skip to second line, returning false if there isn't one
     u = memchr(u, '\n', ulim - u);
@@ -314,7 +314,7 @@ int hts_detect_format(hFILE *hfile, htsFormat *fmt)
     unsigned char s[2048];
     ssize_t len = hpeek(hfile, s, sizeof s);
     ...
-    if (len >= 2 && s[0] == '>' && secondline_is_bases(s, s+len))
+    if (len >= 2 && s[0] == '>' && is_fastaq(s, s+len))
         fmt->format = fasta_format;
-    else if (len >= 2 && s[0] == '@' && secondline_is_bases(s, s+len))
+    else if (len >= 2 && s[0] == '@' && is_fastaq(s, s+len))
         fmt->format = fastq_format;
     ...
}
--END AGENT OBSERVATION--

Let me look at the `colmatch` function and the `parse_tabbed_text` function. The key insight is that the heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 might be in the `colmatch` function when the pattern is shorter than the columns string.

Let me look at the `colmatch` function again:
```c
static int colmatch(const char *columns, const char *pattern)
{
    int i;
    for (i = 0; columns[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (pattern[i] == '+') return i;
        if (! (columns[i] == pattern[i] || pattern[i] == 'Z')) return 0;
    }
    return i;
}
```

The loop continues while `columns[i] != '\0'`. For the shorter patterns like `"iiiiii"` (6 chars), if `columns` has more than 6 chars, then at i=6, `columns[6] != '\0'`, so we check `pattern[6]`. `pattern[6]` is the NUL terminator. `pattern[i] == '+'`? No. `columns[i] == pattern[i] || pattern[i] == 'Z'`? `pattern[6]` is '\0', so `columns[i] == '\0'`? No (columns[6] is some char). `pattern[6] == 'Z'`? No. So returns 0. No overflow.

Author: John Marshall <jmarshall@hey.com>

    Recognise FASTA/Q even if the file has a very long header file
